questions.answer: In searching for, interpreting or remembering evidence.
questions.feedback: Check the definition and explain it in your own words before retrying.

questions.prompt: Does a true belief rule out biased reasoning?
questions.answer: No; the process can be biased even when the conclusion is correct.
questions.feedback: Check the distinction or calculation against the worked case; correct the first unsupported step.

questions.prompt: What makes an evidence search discriminating?
questions.answer: It seeks observations that competing explanations predict differently.
questions.feedback: State a concrete implication or limitation and retry without notes.

scoring.knowledge: 1 point per correct answer; formative only.
scoring.practice: Identifies selective handling of evidence and designs a symmetric test.
scoring.transfer: Choose a fictional preference between two products. Build an evidence table with three observations for each position and a written revision condition. Review the table tomorrow.
scoring.pass: All mapped criteria require Level 2 evidence; quiz score alone is insufficient.
